raw_html:
Equivalent qualifications for United States of America

One of the following will be considered: 

  • 5,5,4 in three distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.
  • 5,4 in two distinctive AP subjects, plus a combined score of 1400 in the SAT or a composite score of 31 in the ACT taken in the final three years of high school. The successful completion of the High School Graduation Diploma also required.
  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent). 

Please see 'A Levels' for subject requirements. Where A* is required at A Level, 5 will be required in the relevant full-year AP subject; for A, 5 will be required; and for B, 4 will be required. Where Mathematics or Physics is required, applicants will be asked to present specific AP subjects. 

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

One of the following will be considered: 

  • 5,5,4 in three distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.
  • 5,4 in two distinctive AP subjects, plus a combined score of 1400 in the SAT or a composite score of 31 in the ACT taken in the final three years of high school. The successful completion of the High School Graduation Diploma also required.
  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent). 

Please see 'A Levels' for subject requirements. Where A* is required at A Level, 5 will be required in the relevant full-year AP subject; for A, 5 will be required; and for B, 4 will be required. Where Mathematics or Physics is required, applicants will be asked to present specific AP subjects. 

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

department: School of Slavonic and East European Studies
description: Join 11 million native speakers by learning Czech from leading experts, while taking advantage of our well-equipped language learning suites and libraries. Enhance your future career prospects by achieving near-native proficiency in Italian, while making the most of UCL’s top language learning facilities. Our Czech and Italian degree is taught across two departments; the School of Slavonic and East European Studies (SSEES) and the School of European Languages, Culture and Society (SELCS), and offers huge scope for developing in-depth, comparative and intercultural approaches to the humanities. You will be able to choose from a wide range of modules including literature, linguistic traditions, history, sociology, philosophy, art, film or other aspects of the cultures associated with the languages you'll be learning.

ib_subjects: A total of 17 points in three higher level subjects to include a foreign language, with no higher level score below 5.

raw_html:
Equivalent qualifications for United States of America

One of the following will be considered: 

  • 5,5,5 in three distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.
  • 5,4 in two distinctive AP subjects, plus a combined score of 1440 in the SAT or a composite score of 32 in ACT taken in the final three years of high school. The successful completion of the High School Graduation Diploma also required.
  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent).  

Please see 'A Levels' for subject requirements. Where A* is required at A Level, 5 will be required in the relevant full-year AP subject; for A, 5 will be required; and for B, 4 will be required. Where Mathematics or Physics is required, applicants will be asked to present specific AP subjects. 

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

title: German and Russian BA
subject: Languages and Culture Studies - Russian and East European
department: School of Slavonic and East European Studies
description: Gain excellent linguistic competence in German while deepening your knowledge of Germanic literature, history and film. Become fluent in Russian and deepen your understanding of the history, culture and geopolitics of a vast region. Our German and Russian degree is taught across two departments; the School of Slavonic and East European Studies (SSEES) and the School of European Languages, Culture and Society (SELCS), and offers huge scope for developing in-depth, comparative and intercultural approaches to the humanities. You will be able to choose from a wide range of modules including literature, linguistic traditions, history, sociology, philosophy, art, film or other aspects of the cultures associated with the languages you'll be learning.

ib_subjects: A total of 16 in three higher level subjects to include a foreign language, with no higher level score below 5.

Reading and Discussion of Texts in Russian

  • 5,5,4 in three distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.

  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent).

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

One of the following will be considered: 

  • 5,5,5,5,4 in five distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.
  • 5,5 in two distinctive AP subjects, plus a combined score of 1470 in the SAT or a composite score of 33 in ACT taken in the final three years of high school. The successful completion of the High School Graduation Diploma also required.
  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent).

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

Equivalent qualifications for United States of America

One of the following will be considered: 

  • 5,5,5,5 in four distinctive AP subjects, taken in the final three years of high school.
  • 5,5 in two distinctive AP subjects, plus a combined score of 1440 in the SAT or a composite score of 32 in ACT taken in the final three years of high school. The successful completion of the High School Graduation Diploma also required.
  • The successful completion of one year of study at a recognised US university, Community or Junior College, with an overall CGPA of 3.3/4.0 (equivalent to a 2.1) may also be considered. We expect applicants to complete around 30 semester credits (or equivalent). 

Please see 'A Levels' for subject requirements. Where A* is required at A Level, 5 will be required in the relevant full-year AP subject; for A, 5 will be required; and for B, 4 will be required. Where Mathematics or Physics is required, applicants will be asked to present specific AP subjects. 

AP exam scores must be verified by the College Board and sent to UCL through the College Board directly. 

For further information on the required subjects, please refer to United States of America. If you are unsure whether you satisfy the subject requirements, please contact Undergraduate Admissions for advice.

title: History and Philosophy of Science BSc
subject: Science and Technology Studies
faculty: Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences
department: Science and Technology Studies
description: This humanities degree examines the past and present of science, technology and medicine, as well as their global complexity. Travelling from voyages of exploitation, through debates about evolution, and into the design of next-generation pharmaceuticals, students discover how science has shaped our world and where we might go next. We combine approaches from history, philosophy, art and religion to ask important questions: Who makes knowledge? When is research unethical? What is good evidence for a theory?
